simple.meaning: פִּלְאִי (pilʼîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “remarkable.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּלְאִי (H6383) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 13:18, with occurrences in Judges, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּלְאִי (H6383) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּלְאִי (H6383) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּלְאִי (pilʼîy) / H6383 is traced through Judges 13:18, Psalms 139:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6383. pili or pali [ מָּלִיא ] see following. [ מִּלְאִי ] adjective wonderful, incomprehensible ; — masculine פלאי (i.e. מִּלְאִי ) Kt, Judg 13:18 (name of י ׳מַלְאַךְ ; > Qr מֶּ֫לִי(אׅ ); feminine מִמֶּנִּי דַעַת פלאיה (i.e. מִּלְאִיָה ) Psa 139:6 God's knowledge; > Qr מְּלִיאָה .

occurrences.englishText: Yahweh’s angel said to him, “Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible* or, wonderful?”
